messages:
ryan_sales: LibertyHealth wants to run a short POC next week using a finetuned Llama-3-70B (quantized). They need: catalog compatibility, KV/cache behavior for ~2k seq, and a month-of-usage pricing for ~200k tokens/day. They also asked about HIPAA & KMS. Link to their questionnaire: https://libertyhealth.example/qna

maya_se: On it. @jordan_eng can you do a quick compatibility scan? main checks: tokenizer parity, quantization format (q8 vs q4), and whether our runtime supports the adapter layers they shipped. Also confirm Dedicated vs Hosted options.

jordan_eng: Quick notes after initial repo glance: base Llama-3-70B loads but their finetuned adapters are an HF repo with custom tokenizer files. If tokenizer != standard we need to bundle it. Quant note: our current hosted kernels reliably support q8_0 for 70B; q4 variants need the newer kernel (not yet in prod). I'll run a small local test: 
```
# quick tokenizer check
python3 -c "from transformers import AutoTokenizer; print(AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('liberty/llama3-70b-ft').bos_token)"
```
If that fails, we'll request the tokenizer bundle from the customer.

maya_se: Good — please flag any tokenizer mismatches ASAP. If they used SentencePiece with nonstandard special tokens we need the mapping.

anna_security: LibertyHealth requires HIPAA controls, per-request audit logging, and key rotation with a customer-managed KMS. Private deployment preferred but Dedicated in us-east with strict network isolation might be acceptable. I'll attach our HIPAA checklist and the dataflow diagram they asked for. Need confirmation from product on audit-log retention options.

liz_acct: For pricing ballpark: 200k tokens/day ~ 6M tokens/mo. Two paths: Hosted (per-token) vs Dedicated (reserved GPUs + infra). Ballpark numbers: hosted generation heavy with 70B quant → estimate ~$0.012/token gen + $0.001/token context (very rough). Dedicated reserved (1x A100-equivalent pool with quant kernels) ~ $13k/mo commit + infra and support. I'll run exact calc once we know batch sizes and expected RPS. @ryan_sales can you confirm expected concurrency?

oliver_ops: KV cache: at 2k seq, per-session KV ~150–220MB depending on kv dtype. If sessions are long-lived and we can reuse prefix cache, caching will reduce compute by ~30–60%. Recommend enabling prefix caching + autoscale min workers for the POC. Also note: for q8 we see stable latency; q4 rollout requires kernel update (see @jordan_eng).

jordan_eng: Confirming kernel status: q4f32 for 70B depends on new Triton kernels and a runtime patch. We can push the kernel to a Dedicated pool but timeline ~3 business days to schedule and validate. If customer can accept q8_0 we can start perf runs today.

maya_se: Next steps checklist: 1) @ryan_sales get model repo + tokenizer bundle + sample prompt set (10–20 prompts) 2) customer to confirm if HIPAA requires Private or Dedicated 3) @liz_acct will produce a month estimate after we get expected concurrency/batch sizes 4) @jordan_eng will spin a short perf test on a Dedicated trial slot (q8 path) 5) @anna_security will send the HIPAA checklist and intake form to Liberty.

ryan_sales: I'll collect the repo and prompts and ask Liberty to confirm deployment mode (Private vs Dedicated). I'll push the questionnaire today — they want kickoff Mon.

ops-bot: Ticket created: SALES-12345 "LibertyHealth POC - Llama3-70B compatibility & pricing" assigned to maya_se, jordan_eng, anna_security, liz_acct. ETA: triage today. :white_check_mark:
